newsitem.title: PERU: Peru sees lower '97 balance of payments deficit.
newsitem.headline: Peru sees lower '97 balance of payments deficit.

text.p: Peru's Economy Ministry said Tuesday the country's current account balance of payments deficit was expected to decline to the equivalent of 5.3 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) this year from 5.8 percent in 1996.
The government aims for a 5.0 percent balance of payments' deficit in 1998, an economy ministry spokeswoman said.

Regarding Peru's fiscal outlook, she said the ministry forecast the primary surplus of the government would fall to 1.3 percent of GDP this year from 1.5 percent in 1996. The central bank defines the primary surplus as the difference between revenues and expenditures excluding interest payments on debt.
The government is aiming for a 2.0 percent primary surplus in 1998, according to the ministry spokeswoman.
Annualized inflation was also following a downward trend and would reach 9.2 percent in March from 9.4 percent in February, according to the ministry.
